the (K1− z Naz)xFe2− y Se2 system is a superconducting material with a two-gap superconducting order parameter, with a large gap ΔL ≈ 9 meV and a small one ΔS ≈ 2 meV, with a large anisotropy ratio ΔL/ΔS ≈ 4.7.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have grown single crystals of (K1− zNaz)xFe2 −y Se2 with high-quality superconductivity.
we have grown single crystals with a large superconducting gap, which is consistent with the two-gap model.
(K1−xNax)0.3Fe1.8Se1.5 single crystals exhibit a two-gap superconducting state with a small gap ΔS = 1.9 meV and a large gap ΔL = 9.3 meV, and that the large gap is the driving condensate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (K1−xNax)Fe2Se2 system exhibits two superconducting gaps with the large gap being the driving one.
the (K1− zNaz)xFe2 − ySe2 crystals are superconductors with two superconducting gaps, which can be explained in terms of the BCS theory with a strong coupling constant.
the mixed alkali-metal (K1−xNaz)xFe2Se2 single crystals can be grown by the self-flux method and the two gap superconductivity is present in the as-prepared crystals.
